newsitem.title: USA: Treasury's Hawke optimistic on thrift fund fix.
newsitem.headline: Treasury's Hawke optimistic on thrift fund fix.

text.p: Treasury Undersecretary John Hawke said Thursday he was "very optimistic" about prospects for passage of legislation to bolster the fund that insures deposits at thrifts.
"I'm very optimistic about the prospects of getting it through," Hawke told reporters at a banking conference.
"There's a growing awareness (in Congress) that the way to get it through is to trim down the package to a scope that everybody can agree with," Hawke said.
The way to pass the proposal, which would bolster the Savings Association Insurance Fund, would be to leave off controversial provisions, he said.
House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach has said Republicans are considering attaching the thrift insurance fund legislation to a continuing resolution, a short-term spending bill.
But he said he did not know what bill the legislation might be attached to.
He said the reason he is optimistic that the legislation will pass is that, otherwise, Congress will have to address the issue next year in a "crisis" context.
